text.p: The following are top stories from selected Singapore newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Singapore Prime Minister Goh Chok Tong declares General Election issue is opposition Workers' Party candidate Tang Liang Hong and determines to stop Tang from getting into Parliament.
- Workers' Party candidate Tang is not seeking court injunction to stop People's Action Party leaders from calling him anti-Christian Chinese chauvinist.
- Computer scientist fined for retrieving data from chief financial officer's electronic mailbox and faxing copies to company's clients.
- Indonesian-born businesmsan to bail out debt-laden videotape maker Electro-Magnetic in potential deal that will value EML shares at Singapore 16.8 cents apiece.
- Chinese economy estimated to grow by 9.7 percent this year.
- Swiss chemical firm Lonza in joint venture with Economic Development Board with investment of U.S. $125 million in chemical plant in Singapore.
- U.S. dollar hits 44-month high of 116.18 yen amid concern investors will shun Japanese investments into new year.
- Goldron's Malaysian subsidiary Measurex Corporation Bhd receives in-principle approval to list on Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange's Second Board.
- Cam International Holdings suffers 59.9 percent drop in after-tax profit to Singapore $3.36 million for full year ended September 30.
- Creative Technology shares surge Singapore $0.70 on main board to $14.10.
- Yamaichi Research Institute expects Singapore's electronics stocks to rise next year, boosted by growing United States electronics demand.
- Industrial equipment supplier Causeway Investment undergoes some changes in top management.
